decisionLog.outcome: Reset 2.2.2 under Andrew Wright, retiring the inherited delivery steps and resource assumptions and redrafting the proposition around partnership infrastructure, access funding, alumni and philanthropy. The proposition is now ready for informal stakeholder sense-check before formal Delivery design.

Rebased the recommended Core planning assumption for partnership infrastructure from £600,000 to £400,000 p.a. from 2027/28, while preserving Year 1 discovery and the requirement to produce lean, Core and more ambitious operating-model options from evidence. Student Opportunities Fund design remains within 2.2.2, but any new award pot is explicitly outside the King's Edge mobilisation ask and requires a separate institutional, consolidated-fund, philanthropic or other funding route.

decisionLog.forum: King's Edge Delivery Plan working update
decisionLog.outcome: Broaden 2.2.2 into Future-Proofed Employability & Experiential Infrastructure. Preserve the existing experiential partnership, access-funding, alumni and philanthropy work; add dedicated international employer-engagement, proactive graduate-transition and incremental global-mobility opportunity-development capability; and model the UK Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development investment from 2027/28 as four specified posts: 1 x G6 Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development Manager, 2 x G5 Experiential Opportunity Development Advisers and 1 x G5 Experiential Partnerships Operations & Intelligence Adviser. On the current fully loaded role-cost basis this remains £214,089 annualised, matching the fully developed international employer-engagement team. Andrew Wright leads the deliverable with Eleanor Hannan as co-lead. Graduate Transitions is deferred to September 2028, bringing the G7 Head and G6 Coach into the final investment year. Global Mobility opportunity-development capacity remains planned as 1 x G6 plus 1 x G5 from September 2027. All grade-based staffing figures are treated as fully loaded planning costs including employer National Insurance and pension/superannuation, subject to Finance/HR validation before approval.

Apply a hard mobilisation boundary of 2026/27 to 2028/29. Bring the final two international Employer Relations & Insights G5 posts forward into the final investment year, with a January 2029 planning start after the East Asia G5 and Graduate Transitions team mobilise in September 2028. The full 2.2.2 operating model must therefore be live by June 2029, with £714,058 as the fully mobilised annualised exit run-rate. Activity after June 2029 is benefits realisation, evaluation and business-as-usual settlement rather than new mobilisation investment.

Replace annualised run-rates in the three-year investment arithmetic with explicit in-year planning budgets. Assume September starts are funded for ten months of the relevant academic year and January 2029 starts for six months, while the £50,000 international non-pay envelope is budgeted in full in each active year. On this basis 2.2.2 requires £0 new direct investment in 2026/27, £367,569 in 2027/28 and £632,071 in 2028/29, a three-year direct profile of £999,640. The £714,058 figure remains the fully mobilised annualised exit run-rate, not an in-year budget. Exact payroll and on-costs remain subject to Finance/HR validation.
